# GitLab Pages CI

Use GitLab 17.10 or newer and a Linux Docker runner to build a Great Docs site.
The Pages job publishes the default branch. The merge-request job retains the
rendered site as an artefact and leaves the production site unchanged.

## Pipeline recipe

Create `.gitlab-ci.yml` at the package root. This example uses an existing
`docs/great-docs.yml` and installs the package with uv:

```{.yaml filename=".gitlab-ci.yml"}
.docs-build:
  image: python:3.12-bookworm
  stage: build
  variables:
    GIT_DEPTH: "0"
    QUARTO_VERSION: "1.11.9"
  before_script:
    - apt-get update && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends curl ca-certificates
    - |
      case "$(uname -m)" in
        x86_64) quarto_arch=amd64 ;;
        aarch64|arm64) quarto_arch=arm64 ;;
        *) echo "Unsupported architecture" >&2; exit 1 ;;
      esac
      curl --fail --location --output /tmp/quarto.tar.gz "https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-cli/releases/download/v${QUARTO_VERSION}/quarto-${QUARTO_VERSION}-linux-${quarto_arch}.tar.gz"
      tar -xzf /tmp/quarto.tar.gz -C /opt
      ln -s "/opt/quarto-${QUARTO_VERSION}/bin/quarto" /usr/local/bin/quarto
    - curl --fail --location --output /tmp/install-uv.sh https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh
    - env UV_UNMANAGED_INSTALL=/usr/local/bin sh /tmp/install-uv.sh
    - uv venv
    - uv pip install -e . great-docs
  script:
    - uv run --no-sync great-docs build

great-docs-pages:
  extends: .docs-build
  pages:
    publish: docs/_site
  rules:
    - if: '$CI_PIPELINE_SOURCE == "push" && $CI_COMMIT_BRANCH == $CI_DEFAULT_BRANCH'

great-docs-preview:
  extends: .docs-build
  rules:
    - if: '$CI_PIPELINE_SOURCE == "merge_request_event"'
  after_script:
    - |
      if [ "$CI_JOB_STATUS" = success ]; then
        uv run --no-sync great-docs ci gitlab-notice --job "$CI_JOB_ID" --mr "$CI_MERGE_REQUEST_IID"
        if [ "${GREAT_DOCS_MR_COMMENT:-false}" = true ]; then
          uv run --no-sync great-docs ci mr-comment --job "$CI_JOB_ID" --mr "$CI_MERGE_REQUEST_IID"
        fi
      fi
  artifacts:
    name: docs-html
    paths: [docs/_site]
    expire_in: 1 week
```

The checked-in `gitlab-ci-template.yml` asset supplies the same job structure to
the setup command. [GitLab's Pages syntax](https://docs.gitlab.com/ci/yaml/#pagespublish)
requires a publish path relative to the checkout root and a non-empty `index.html`.
GitLab 17.10 adds that path to the job's artefacts automatically.

The runner installs [Quarto's Linux tarball](https://quarto.org/docs/download/tarball.html)
and [uv's standalone installer](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/getting-started/installation/).
Change `QUARTO_VERSION` to select another supported Quarto release. Add system
dependencies required by your notebooks to `before_script`.

## Setup command

Generate the pipeline from the selected project's Python requirement, lock file
and output layout:

```{.bash filename="Terminal"}
great-docs setup-gitlab-pages
great-docs setup-gitlab-pages --config website/settings.yml
great-docs setup-gitlab-pages --main-branch develop --python-version 3.12
great-docs setup-gitlab-pages --package-manager uv
```

The command detects uv and Poetry lock files and otherwise installs the package
and documentation extras through uv's pip interface. It uses Python 3.11 or newer
and retains an explicit Python-version choice. The default deployment rule reads
`CI_DEFAULT_BRANCH`; `--main-branch` selects an explicit deployment branch.

If `.gitlab-ci.yml` already exists, the command prints a snippet for merging and
leaves the file intact. Add its jobs to your pipeline and add `build` to a custom
`stages` list, or change the jobs' stage to one already present. Use `--force` to
replace the existing file.

## Site addresses

During a GitLab CI build, Great Docs uses
[`CI_PAGES_URL`](https://docs.gitlab.com/ci/variables/predefined_variables/)
when `site_url` is absent. An explicit `site_url` wins. An independent
`seo.canonical.base_url` continues to control canonical links. Local project
discovery does not infer a GitLab Pages address.

The generated pipeline publishes the selected layout's final site directory.
For `website/settings.yml`, it publishes `website/_site`; for an unmigrated
root configuration, it publishes `great-docs/_site`. Versioned builds publish
the assembled root, including historical versions under `v/`.

## Deployment check

Commit the reviewed pipeline and run it on your GitLab instance. Open
**Deploy > Pages** to find the deployed address. Verify the homepage, an API
page, a nested guide, assets and canonical links, including any URL subdirectory.
Inspect the merge-request artefact separately to confirm that its build does
not deploy production Pages.

The pipeline and output layout have local coverage. Live Pages deployment
acceptance remains pending until those checks run on an authorised GitLab
project. The generated pipeline posts no merge-request note by default.


## Local previews

Download the documentation archive by its job ID without requiring access to job
metadata. Select a pipeline or an MR when metadata access is available:

```{.bash filename="Terminal"}
great-docs preview --repo https://gitlab.com/group/package --job 12345
great-docs preview --repo https://gitlab.com/group/package --pipeline 6789
great-docs preview --repo https://gitlab.com/group/package --mr 42
great-docs preview --provider gitlab --repo group/package --mr 42
```

Pass `--artifact` with the documentation job or archive name when several jobs
publish archives. A missing or expired archive needs a new documentation build.
GitHub selectors `--pr`, `--run`, `--branch` and `--use-gh` retain their meanings.

Set `GITLAB_TOKEN` with `read_api` access for private artifacts and MR/pipeline
metadata. Anonymous access works for public artifacts when the project permits it.
A permitted `CI_JOB_TOKEN` can download job artifacts; it cannot discover pipelines
or jobs or post notes. GitLab tokens stay on the GitLab origin during CDN redirects.

For self-managed installations, specify the provider and preserve any HTTP prefix:

```{.bash filename="Terminal"}
great-docs preview --provider gitlab \
  --repo https://code.example.org/gitlab/team/subteam/package \
  --repo-base-url https://code.example.org/gitlab --job 12345
```

## Opt-in notes

The generated jobs always print ordinary job-log instructions. Enable sticky MR
notes only for trusted pipelines by setting `GREAT_DOCS_MR_COMMENT=true` and supplying
`GITLAB_TOKEN` with API write permissions and access to the target MR. Keep write
credentials out of untrusted contributor builds. A CI job token cannot post notes.
Run the note command from a trusted job when contributor code requires isolation.

```{.bash filename="Terminal"}
great-docs ci gitlab-notice --job 12345 --mr 42 \
  --repo https://gitlab.com/team/package
great-docs ci mr-comment --job 12345 --mr 42 \
  --repo https://gitlab.com/team/package \
  --artifact-repo https://gitlab.com/contributor/package
```

Use `--repo` for the MR target and `--artifact-repo` for the project that owns the
built job. Both share the same instance base. In GitLab CI, the commands use
`CI_MERGE_REQUEST_PROJECT_URL` for the target and `CI_PROJECT_URL` for the job owner.
They derive the base from `CI_API_V4_URL` unless an explicit configured base is
preserved by the generated command. Note lookup follows pagination and updates the
existing preview marker; reruns update that note instead of adding another.
